title: Dividends — s 44 ITAA 1936
summary: Facet map: is a company payment assessable under s 44? Spine: s 6(1) 'dividend' definition → paid out of profits (s 44(1A)/(1B) deeming) → demerger dividend exception (s 44(2)-(6)) → residency split (s 44(1)(a) resident/worldwide, (b) non-resident/Australian-source + WHT, (c) non-resident through Australian PE) → displacement by other provisions (s 23AI, s 23AK, s 128D, s 768-5, Div 802). FACETS: non-share dividends (s 974-115), returns of capital vs dividends (TR 2012/5), conduit foreign income (Div 802), dividend WHT (s 128B — franked exemption s 128B(3)(ga), treaty rates), franking/imputation (Div 207), other deemed dividends (s 47, s 47A, Div 7A). Subsection coverage: s 44(1)(a)-(c), (1A), (1B), (2)-(7) mapped; s 6(1) 'dividend' mapped to the first decision. Rulings: TR 2003/8, PS LA 2008/10, TD 1995/50, TR 2012/5, PCG 2018/8.

nodes.label: A company pays you an amount as a shareholder — is it assessable under s 44?
nodes.body: Single question with facets. Spine: is it a dividend (s 6(1)) → paid out of profits → demerger → residency → other provisions. Facets carry the niche definitional and deeming rules.

nodes.label: Is the amount a dividend within the s 6(1) definition?
nodes.body: s 6(1) 'dividend' includes: (a) any distribution made by a company to any of its shareholders, whether in money or other property; and (b) any amount credited by a company to any of its shareholders as shareholders. BUT does NOT include: (d) moneys/property debited against the share capital account (subject to s 6(4)); (e) moneys/property for redemption/cancellation of a redeemable preference share (except any excess over the amount paid-up); PLUS includes: (f) a reversionary bonus on a life assurance policy. The 'paid out of profits' condition is a separate s 44(1) requirement, not part of the s 6(1) definition. Non-share dividends are not within this definition but are caught by s 44(1)(a)(ii)/(b)(ii)/(c)(ii) and s 974-115 ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: Not a dividend — s 44 does not apply
nodes.body: Outside the s 6(1) definition (genuine return of capital, non-shareholder payment). Consider CGT and Div 7A for private company payments.

nodes.label: Was the dividend paid out of profits (considering s 44(1A)/(1B) deemings)?
nodes.body: s 44(1)(a)(i) requires dividends to be paid out of profits. s 44(1A): A dividend paid out of an amount OTHER than profits is taken to be a dividend paid out of profits (deeming rule). s 44(1B): Where (a) the dividend is debited against the share capital account, or (b) the dividend is a repayment of an amount paid-up on a share, the dividend is deemed to have been paid out of profits. Note: The s 6(1)(d) exclusion for share capital account debits and the s 6(4) modification interact with the s 44(1B) deeming.

nodes.label: Are you a resident or non-resident shareholder?
nodes.body: s 44(1)(a) resident: dividends from ANY-source profits + all non-share dividends. s 44(1)(b) non-resident: only Australian-source profits (and non-share dividends from Australian sources). s 44(1)(c) non-resident with an Australian PE of a resident company: dividends attributable to the PE from foreign-source profits.

nodes.label: Assessable to resident — worldwide profits (s 44(1)(a))
nodes.body: Dividends from any source + all non-share dividends. Franking credits attach under Div 207 ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: Non-resident — does the shareholder carry on business through an Australian PE? (s 44(1)(c))
nodes.body: s 44(1)(b): For non-resident shareholders, dividends are assessable only to the extent paid out of Australian-source profits. s 44(1)(c): If the non-resident carries on business through an Australian PE of a RESIDENT company, dividends attributable to the PE from foreign-source profits are also assessable. Note: s 128B and s 128D ITAA 1936 deal with dividend withholding tax.

nodes.label: Is the company a resident and does the shareholder have an Australian PE? (s 44(1)(c))
nodes.body: s 44(1)(c): Applies only if (1) the shareholder is a non-resident carrying on business through an Australian PE, AND (2) the company is a RESIDENT. Dividends (other than non-share dividends) attributable to the PE are assessable to the extent paid out of profits derived from sources OUTSIDE Australia (s 44(1)(c)(i)). Non-share dividends attributable to the PE are assessable to the extent derived from sources outside Australia (s 44(1)(c)(ii)). PE meaning follows the DTA (s 44(7)(a)) or s 6(1) (s 44(7)(b)). If the company is non-resident, s 44(1)(c) does not apply.

nodes.label: Assessable to the extent attributable to the PE (s 44(1)(c))
nodes.body: s 44(1)(c)(i): Foreign-source dividends (other than non-share dividends) attributable to the Australian PE of a resident company are assessable. s 44(1)(c)(ii): Non-share dividends attributable to the PE from foreign sources are also assessable.

nodes.label: Does another provision expressly deal with the dividend?
nodes.body: s 44(1) yields to provisions that expressly include/exclude dividends: s 23AI (foreign company dividends), s 23AK, s 128D ITAA 1936 (WHT-exempt — s 128D: income subject to WHT is not assessable), s 768-5 ITAA 1997 (NANE participation exemption), Div 802 conduit foreign income.

nodes.label: Dividend included in assessable income (s 44)
nodes.body: Included under s 44, subject to franking gross-up (Div 207 ITAA 1997) and any specific exclusion.

nodes.label: FACET — Non-share dividends (s 974-115 ITAA 1997)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 974-115 ITAA 1997 (non-share dividends — returns on non-share equity interests); s 44(1)(a)(ii)/(b)(ii). Non-share dividends are assessable regardless of the profits test. The distinction matters for hybrid instruments (convertible notes, non-share equity interests).

nodes.label: FACET — Returns of capital vs dividends
nodes.body: Where to look: s 6(1) 'dividend' exclusion for returns of capital not out of profits; CGT consequences (return of capital reduces cost base; excess is a capital gain — CGT event C2/G1); TR 2012/5 (s 254T Corporations Act — when a company is taken to have paid a dividend). The s 44(1B) deeming catches debits to the share capital account that are in substance distributions of profits.

rulings.title: section 254T of the Corporations Act and the assessment and franking of dividends

nodes.label: FACET — Conduit foreign income (Div 802 ITAA 1997)
nodes.body: Where to look: Div 802 ITAA 1997. An amount declared conduit foreign income is not included in assessable income under s 44(1)(b) or (c) (s 44 note). This lets Australian companies flow foreign-source profits to non-resident shareholders without Australian dividend tax.

nodes.label: FACET — Dividend withholding tax (s 128B ITAA 1936)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 128B ITAA 1936; TD 1995/50. Rate 30% (s 128B(1)); treaty-reduced to 15% (portfolio) or 5% (related company with >=10% holding). Franked dividends to non-residents: exempt from WHT (s 128B(3)(ga)) and the franking credit is not refundable. s 128D ITAA 1936: amounts subject to WHT are not otherwise assessable.

nodes.label: FACET — Franking and imputation (Div 207 ITAA 1997)
nodes.body: Where to look: Div 207 ITAA 1997; TR 2012/5; PCG 2018/8 (incorrect franking). Franked distributions are grossed up (s 207-20) and the franking credit offsets tax (s 207-20(2)); excess credits are refundable to most taxpayers. Benchmark rule and franking deficit tax apply to the company (Div 203/205 ITAA 1997). Loss companies and non-residents have special rules.

nodes.label: FACET — Other deemed dividends (s 47, s 47A, Div 7A)
nodes.body: Where to look: s 47 ITAA 1936 (liquidator distributions), s 47A ITAA 1936 (CFC distribution benefits — see the separate map), Div 7A ITAA 1936 (private company payments/loans treated as dividends); CCH 'other-deemed-dividends'. Each deeming provision feeds into s 44 assessability.

nodes.label: Is the amount a non-share dividend under s 974-115 ITAA 1997?
nodes.body: Non-share dividends are returns on non-share equity interests (s 974-115 ITAA 1997). They are NOT within the s 6(1) 'dividend' definition but are nonetheless assessable under s 44(1)(a)(ii) (resident — all non-share dividends), s 44(1)(b)(ii) (non-resident — Australian-source non-share dividends), and s 44(1)(c)(ii) (non-resident with Australian PE of a resident company — foreign-source non-share dividends attributable to the PE).

nodes.label: Is the shareholder a resident?
nodes.body: Non-share dividends: s 44(1)(a)(ii) — resident shareholders: ALL non-share dividends are assessable. s 44(1)(b)(ii) — non-resident: only to extent derived from Australian sources. s 44(1)(c)(ii) — non-resident with Australian PE of a resident company: foreign-source non-share dividends attributable to the PE.

nodes.label: Is the non-share dividend derived from Australian sources?
nodes.body: s 44(1)(b)(ii): non-share dividends paid to a non-resident are assessable only to the extent derived from sources in Australia. If derived from foreign sources, go to the PE test (s 44(1)(c)(ii)).

nodes.label: Non-share dividend — not assessable under s 44(1)(b)
nodes.body: Non-share dividend paid to a non-resident, derived from foreign sources, and no Australian PE of a resident company. Not assessable under s 44(1)(b)(ii). Consider PE path (s 44(1)(c)(ii)) or other provisions (Div 7A, etc.).

nodes.label: Is it a demerger dividend (s 44(2)-(6))?
nodes.body: A demerger dividend is a dividend that satisfies the demerger requirements under Subdiv 125-B ITAA 1997. If yes, go to the s 44(2) election check and s 44(5) 50% business-assets test.

nodes.label: Has the head entity elected out under s 44(2)?
nodes.body: s 44(2): Subsections (3) and (4) apply to a demerger dividend UNLESS the head entity elects in writing, within one month after it decides which shareholders will receive ownership interests, that those subsections do not apply. If elected out, the demerger dividend is treated as a normal dividend (assessable under s 44(1)).

nodes.label: Does the demerged entity meet the 50% business-assets test (s 44(5)-(6))?
nodes.body: s 44(5): Subsections (3) and (4) do not apply to a demerger dividend unless, just after the demerger, CGT assets owned by the demerged entity or a demerger subsidiary representing at least 50% by market value of all CGT assets owned by the demerged entity and its demerger subsidiaries are used directly or indirectly in one or more businesses carried on by one or more of those entities. s 44(6): Disregard ownership interests in a demerger subsidiary unless they are used in a business referred to in s 44(5).

nodes.label: Demerger dividend — not assessable (s 44(4))
nodes.body: s 44(3): This section applies to the demerger dividend as if it had not been paid out of profits. s 44(4): A demerger dividend is not assessable income or exempt income. Cost base adjusted under Subdiv 125-B ITAA 1997.

nodes.label: Is the dividend paid out of Australian-source profits?
nodes.body: s 44(1)(b)(i): For a non-resident shareholder, dividends (other than non-share dividends) are assessable only to the extent paid out of profits derived by the company from sources in Australia. If paid out of foreign-source profits, the dividend is not assessable under s 44(1)(b) — but may be assessable under s 44(1)(c) if the shareholder has an Australian PE of a resident company.

nodes.label: Not assessable under s 44(1)(b) — foreign-source profits
nodes.body: Dividend paid to a non-resident out of foreign-source profits. Not assessable under s 44(1)(b)(i). Consider: (a) if the shareholder carries on business through an Australian PE of a resident company, the dividend may be assessable under s 44(1)(c)(i) to the extent attributable to the PE; (b) conduit foreign income (Div 802); (c) dividend WHT (s 128B ITAA 1936) may apply to dividends paid by a resident company.

nodes.label: Is the company a resident?
nodes.body: s 44(1)(c): This paragraph applies only if the company is a resident. If the company is non-resident, s 44(1)(c) does not apply and the foreign-source dividend paid to a non-resident shareholder with an Australian PE is not assessable under s 44.

nodes.label: s 44(1)(c) does not apply — company is non-resident
nodes.body: s 44(1)(c) requires the company to be a resident. A non-resident company paying dividends to a non-resident shareholder through an Australian PE is not caught by s 44(1)(c). Consider other provisions (s 128B, Div 7A, etc.).

nodes.label: FACET — s 44(1A): Dividend paid out of non-profits deemed from profits
nodes.body: s 44(1A): 'For the purposes of this Act, a dividend paid out of an amount other than profits is taken to be a dividend paid out of profits.' This means that even if the source of the dividend is not technically 'profits', it is nonetheless treated as paid out of profits for the purposes of s 44 assessment.

nodes.label: FACET — s 44(1B): Share capital account debits deemed from profits
nodes.body: s 44(1B): Where (a) the dividend is debited against the share capital account, or (b) the dividend is a repayment of an amount paid-up on a share, the dividend is deemed to have been paid out of profits derived by the company. This interacts with the s 6(1)(d) exclusion (share capital account debits not dividends) and s 6(4) (when s 6(1)(d) does not apply).
